cards.explanation: The keeper of the vineyard is the LORD Himself. The speaker says, “I, the LORD, am its keeper…” The LORD holds the job. A vineyard with that keeper is in good hands, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD says, “I guard it night and day…” That covers the whole clock, not just the daylight hours. When the sun goes down, the guarding goes on.
The word is disturb, friends. The LORD says He guards it “…so no one can disturb it…” The guarding has a purpose, and the text names it. Nobody gets to mess with that vineyard.
The answer is True. Right after the guarding, the LORD says, “I am not angry.” That comes in verse 4. A guard who isn't angry, that's worth noticing, friends.

The LORD says He would trample them and burn them down. His words are, “…I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.” He says it about thorns and briers if they confronted Him. Those are strong words, and the text says them plainly.

The answer is that they make peace with Him, friends. The LORD says, “let them make peace with Me…” Right after the thorns and briers, the door is open for peace. The text puts it right there in verse 5.

The answer is that it takes root and fills the world with fruit. The text says, “…Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.” That's a big picture for the days to come, friends. It starts with roots and ends with fruit all over the world.
The answer is True. The text says, “By warfare and exile You contended with her…” This is a heavy part of the passage, friends. The LORD is the one who contended with Israel here.
The word is guilt, friends. The text says, “…Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for…” After all that hardship, this is where it turns. Guilt gets covered, and that's a good word to hear.

The answer is that he makes all the altar stones like crushed chalk. The text says “…makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk…” That's the full fruit of the removal of his sin, friends. And with it, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.

The answer is True. The text says, “There the calves graze, and there they lie down…” The fortified city is deserted, so the calves are the ones grazing there. The city looks very different from a stronghold now, friends.

The reason is that they are a people without understanding, friends. The text says, “for this is a people without understanding.” Then it says their Maker has no compassion on them and their Creator shows them no favor (Isaiah 27:11). I think this one is a hard verse to sit with, and the reason sits right there next to it so nobody has to guess.

The answer is one by one. The text says, “…you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.” The gathering is one by one, and that's the promise the text gives, friends. It's a gathering of Israelites, and the text says it plainly.
The sound is a great ram's horn, friends. The text says, “…a great ram’s horn will sound…” That's the sound in that day. It comes right before those in Assyria and Egypt come forth.

The answer is False. The text says, “…those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt.” They come forth together, from both places, friends. The exiles in Egypt are part of it.
The place is the holy mountain in Jerusalem, friends. The text says, “…they will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.” That's where the passage ends. Worship is where they're headed.
